Classic GANs train a forger against a judge over pixels. **loom-core runs the
same adversarial tension over logic itself.**

- **Generator (Breeder)** — renders candidate implementations of your contract
  from strategy families with form dials and corruption pressure. Three voices:
  `mech` (pure templates, 0 tokens), `sysone` (one batched System One call
  biases the picks), `systwo` (LLM wildcard rewrites on plateau).
- **Discriminator (Forge)** — grows an adversarial probe vector: scar tissue
  from every candidate it killed, twin-mining where elites disagree, quantum-
  salted boundaries when a MOTH vault is present, rare-answer mining.
- **The Sheet** — the probing organ is a *quilt*: candidates are compiled and
  scored INSIDE program cells; listeners crown, scar, and harden as reflexes.
  The GAN is watchable.
- **The Archive** — MAP-Elites-style selection on composite novelty
  (behavioral distance, dominant + structural token 3-gram distance). Every
  generation books into an fnv-1a-64 witness chain. The equilibrium product is
  **an archive of maximally-divergent, proven-correct implementations** —
  durable logic, where every dot of disagreement between elites marks a
  boundary of understanding.

## Quickstart (zero keys, zero network)

```bash
npm run example          # breed 12 generations of the fnv-1a-64 witness idiom
npm test                 # born-correct sweep + sheet reflexes + chain verify
```

Write a contract, get durable logic:

```js
import { Loom, defineContract } from 'loom-core';

export default defineContract({
  id: 'my_thing',
  title: 'My contract',
  spec: 'Precise natural-language contract the forge hunts against.',
  oracle: `function solve(input) { /* reference */ }`,
  canon: (out) => JSON.stringify(out),          // equivalence canonicalizer
  genInput: (R) => ({ /* random VALID input from seeded rng R */ }),
  baseProbes: [ /* hand-forged boundary cases */ ],
  families: [ /* >= 2 strategy templates: render(R, corrupt) -> source */ ],
});

// const loom = await new Loom(target, { seed: 7 }).init();
// await loom.run(24);
// loom.report().elites_src   ← crowned, drop-in implementations
```

## Why "divergent, yet exact"?

An implementation that is exact but structurally identical to the reference
teaches you nothing — it is a mimic. An implementation that is different but
sometimes wrong is a fake. **The loom pays only for the intersection**:
behaviorally exact on the entire adversarial probe vector, structurally alien
from everything ever crowned. The archive is therefore not redundancy — it is
a *population of understanding*, each member a different proof-shape of the
same truth.
